Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd Names New Chief Executive to Steer Growth Strategy

LUSAKA, Zambia, June 12 — Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd, one of Zambia’s leading copper processing companies, has appointed veteran mining executive Charles Mwamba as its new Chief Executive Officer, the company said Wednesday.

Mwamba, 52, succeeds outgoing CEO Lin Hui, who is stepping down after six years at the helm. The appointment is effective July 1, according to a statement issued by Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd.

Company officials said Mwamba brings over 25 years of experience in the metals and mining sector, having previously held senior management roles at several copper processing firms across southern Africa. “We are confident that Mr. Mwamba’s extensive leadership background and deep understanding of the Zambian mining landscape will help drive Chambishi’s next phase of growth,” said board chairperson Ruth Banda in the statement.

Zambia is Africa’s second-largest copper producer, and Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd operates one of the country’s major smelting facilities, with an annual processing capacity of more than 250,000 tonnes, according to industry data.

Mwamba said he looked forward to building on the company’s achievements and strengthening ties with local communities and suppliers. “Chambishi has a proud record, and I am committed to enhancing its operational excellence while supporting Zambia’s broader development goals,” he said.

Industry analysts welcomed the appointment, noting the importance of steady leadership amid strong global demand for copper. “With copper prices remaining robust, experienced management is key to maximizing Zambia’s potential,” said Joseph Phiri, mining analyst at Lusaka-based consultancy Copperline Advisory.

Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd employs more than 800 workers and is a significant contributor to the Copperbelt region’s economy.
